label: EU(7)-PIM: muscle relaxants
title: Centrally acting muscle relaxant in an older person
statement: The EU(7)-PIM list names centrally acting muscle relaxants as potentially inappropriate in older people: carisoprodol, methocarbamol, orphenadrine, baclofen, tizanidine, tetrazepam and cyclobenzaprine. They can cause drowsiness, confusion, memory loss, weakness, low blood pressure on standing and falls, and some have anticholinergic effects. Rehabilitation and botulinum toxin are listed as alternatives. Several of these medicines need a lower or more careful dose when the kidneys work poorly.

plain_summary: Muscle relaxants such as baclofen, orphenadrine and methocarbamol can cause sedation, confusion, weakness, low blood pressure on standing and falls in older people.

medicine_groups.name: Centrally acting muscle relaxants
medicine_groups.note: Count only oral tablets, capsules and liquids. Norgesic is orphenadrine with paracetamol. Carisoprodol, tizanidine, tetrazepam and cyclobenzaprine have no Australian brand listed here. Exclude Bacthecal and Lioresal Intrathecal injections even if recorded in the history. Oral Lioresal remains in the group.

rule_for_models: Suspect a finding when any Group A medicine (carisoprodol, methocarbamol, orphenadrine, baclofen, tizanidine, tetrazepam or cyclobenzaprine) is supplied as an oral tablet, capsule or liquid to a person aged 65 or older. One supply is enough. If age is unknown and the supply otherwise qualifies, report only a possible finding and ask the pharmacist to confirm that the person is 65 or older.
cannot_be_seen: Why the medicine was started (for example muscle spasm or spasticity), kidney function, falls and how much the person takes. Also hospital supplies.
ask_the_gp: Whether the muscle relaxant is still needed, whether rehabilitation or another option could replace it, and the person's risk of falls and confusion.
